name: Leviticus

objectives.text: Identify Leviticus as the book where God teaches His people how to come near to Him because He is holy
Name Aaron and his sons as the priests God chose to serve Him at the tabernacle
Recall that God gave Israel rules about being clean so that they could live near Him
Explain from Leviticus that sin separates people from a holy God and that God provided sacrifices so sinners could be forgiven
Identify the five main offerings of Leviticus and state the basic purpose of each
Explain that holy means set apart for God and describe how Israel was to be set apart from the nations
Retell the ordination of the priests and the judgment on Nadab and Abihu and explain what it shows about approaching God His way
Outline the major sections of Leviticus from the offerings through the holiness laws
Compare clean and unclean animals and distinguish ritual uncleanness from moral sin
Explain the laws for skin disease and purification and connect them to Jesus cleansing a leper
Categorize the appointed feasts of Leviticus 23 by their timing and what each commemorated
Describe the Sabbath year and the Year of Jubilee and explain how they taught that the land belonged to God
Analyze the sequence of the Day of Atonement ceremony and the role of the high priest in it
Explain the neighbor-love commands of Leviticus 19 and show how Jesus uses them to summarize the law
Interpret the command to be holy as God is holy in Leviticus and in its New Testament use
Connect the food laws to Israel's separation from the nations and explain why the New Testament sets them aside
Explain how the two goats of the Day of Atonement together picture both payment for sin and its removal
Summarize the covenant blessings and curses of Leviticus 26 and explain God's promise to remember His covenant
Construct an explanation of substitutionary atonement from the laying on of hands and the shedding of blood in Leviticus
Evaluate how the laws of Leviticus apply to New Testament believers using the Reformed distinction of moral, ceremonial, and judicial law
Defend the Reformed teaching that atonement requires the shedding of blood
Synthesize the priesthood, sacrifices, and Day of Atonement of Leviticus with their fulfillment in Christ as taught in Hebrews

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (holiness, priests, cleanness, five offerings, clean and unclean, feasts, Day of Atonement, be holy, food laws, scapegoat, substitution, applying the Holiness Code, blood, Hebrews). Replaced the vague 'sin is serious' item with an objective on sin and sacrifice. Added missing content: Nadab and Abihu, the book's structure, skin disease and purification, Sabbath year and Jubilee, Leviticus 19 neighbor love, and the covenant blessings and curses of chapter 26. Gave verse-level anchors throughout, swapped the loosely fitting WCF 8.4 for WCF 8.5, WSC Q25, HC Q40 and WCF 19.3-5 where those state the doctrine, and kept WCF 8.4 only for the Hebrews synthesis.
